audit.title: Chainlink Functions Service Limits

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Table rows are self-contained (`Maximum callback gas limit … 300,000`), each answering one implied question. Weak: no opening canonical sentence naming the page's subject before the table.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: One clean table is the right format for limits, but the page is a single H1 with no H2/H3 subsections — nothing to anchor symptom/topic queries to. 551-word single section chunks acceptably as one unit.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Measured 20 numerals, 8 with units — this is the page's core value.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: One external link ([Deno](https://deno.land/)); zero primary-spec links. CBOR row and the 300,000 gas figure could cite sources.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Descriptions are decent but verbose ("The maximum amount of gas that you can set for Chainlink Functions to fulfill your callback function"); no crisp top-line definition of the concept.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, 0 og tags. Head metadata could not be verified — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks; genuinely not needed for a limits table. Scored neutral, not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Facts cover the lifecycle but there are no "how do I…/what is the max…" headings or FAQ; retrieval leans on numeric-match luck rather than phrasing.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent "Chainlink Functions"/"DON" usage, unambiguous prose.

audit.summary: This is a pure reference page: a single well-formed table of Chainlink Functions service limits, dense with concrete quantitative values (300,000 gas, 30 KB request size, 5 HTTP queries, 2160h/72h secret TTL). Its biggest strength is specificity — every row is a liftable fact with units. Its biggest opportunity is discoverability plumbing: zero JSON-LD, missing canonical URL, no visible last-updated date, and no question-phrased entry points, so retrieval depends entirely on the table happening to match a numeric query. Honest verdict: strong data, thin machine-readability and query surface — solid but not agent-optimal.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first canonical lead sentence
recommendations.where: immediately below the H1, before the callout/table
recommendations.issue: page jumps from title straight to a shutdown callout and table; no liftable summary.
recommendations.change: add one sentence, e.g. "Chainlink Functions enforces the following per-request and per-subscription service limits: a 300,000 callback gas cap, 30 KB max request size, 10-second execution time, 5 HTTP requests, and a 5-minute request fulfillment timeout."
recommendations.why: gives engines a single self-contained chunk to quote when the table isn't fully ingested, defending against generic-prior guesses about limits.

recommendations.title: Add question-phrased subheadings grouping the table
recommendations.where: split or precede table sections with H2s
recommendations.issue: single H1, "1 headings" measured — no phrasing matches how devs query.
recommendations.change: add H2 anchors like "What is the maximum callback gas limit?", "How many HTTP requests can a Function make?", "How long can Chainlink Functions source code run?", "How long do DON-hosted secrets last?" — either as section headers over grouped rows or a short FAQ list echoing the table values.
recommendations.why: headings phrased as the exact queries win retrieval that concept-titled table cells lose, even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.where: page `<head>` / frontmatter and a visible byline
recommendations.issue: measured — 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, dateModified absent.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, set `<link rel="canonical">` to the page URL, and surface a visible "Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD" line. Limits change; freshness signals matter here.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness raise parse-trust for agents; a limits page with no date is easily treated as stale.

recommendations.title: Cite primary sources for key limits
recommendations.where: CBOR row, callback gas row, Deno runtime row
recommendations.change: link "encoded request" to the CBOR spec (RFC 8949) and the Deno runtime reference where relevant; keep the existing architecture cross-link.
recommendations.why: inline authoritative links raise citation rate and attributability of the numeric claims.

recommendations.title: Tighten row descriptions into liftable one-liners
recommendations.where: long description cells (e.g. Maximum duration of a request)
recommendations.issue: multi-clause descriptions dilute the quotable core.
recommendations.change: front-load each description with a crisp lead clause ("Request fulfillment timeout — a request that exceeds 5 minutes times out and is not charged."), keeping detail after.
recommendations.why: crisp self-contained statements are lifted verbatim more often than diffuse prose.

antiPatterns: Shutdown callout (`<ChainlinkFunctions callout="shutdown" />`) renders as an unresolved component in the served markdown — confirm it produces meaningful text for crawlers, not an empty element.
No visible date on a page whose values are version-/policy-dependent (staleness risk).
No keyword stuffing, fluff, or broken cross-references — clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level schema/canonical templating likely governs the missing JSON-LD and canonical tag — fix at the template layer, not just this page.
Ensure internal links from related Functions pages (architecture, getting-started) point here as the canonical limits hub to win the "outranked by sibling" scenario.
